Hi Emily — appreciate the SOW, that helps. High level:

- Compact slab (fixed retention SKU): you pre-purchase a retention slab (e.g., 30TB-month, 90TB-month) that covers trace ingestion, index storage, and dashboard query retention. Predictable unit economics and lower per-GB cost. Works well if you have steady traffic and want predictable monthly cost.

- Metered (usage-based): billed on actual GBs retained/queried per month. More flexible for spiky workloads; you pay for what you use but per-GB rates are higher.

Discounting/credits: we typically offer tiered volume discounts on slab commitments (5–20% depending on term and size) and limited credits for pilot months. For combined tracing + dashboards, we can apply a bundle discount if you commit at the account level for 12 months.

I've attached a compact vs metered pricing grid to illustrate the breakpoints and a simple 12-month vs 36-month comparison. Happy to walk through numbers.

—Rafael

Rafael — quick internal notes before we call Observix:

1) For accounts like Observix (Series C, projected steady growth), recommend starting with a 12-month slab at mid-tier (90TB-month) with an option to step up after quarter 2. Keeps TCO predictable and simplifies SRE conversations.

2) Offer a 10% bundling discount if they commit to slab for tracing + dashboards together, or 8% if they pick slab for tracing and metered for dashboards. We can layer an additional 3% credit for a 36-month commit.

3) Be prepared to offer one free month of retention credits during pilot to offset migration validation costs.

I'll join the next call to handle product-level questions.

—Karthik

Emily — attached is a short run-rate table (see sheet "Observix model") showing monthly $ for both options A and B, with effective per-GB rates. Highlights:

- Option A (both slabs): lower per-GB cost for dashboards (~$0.045/GB effective) and overall predictability. Monthly run-rate = $24,600 (example).
- Option B (metered dashboards): dashboard per-GB = $0.078/GB given usage patterns; monthly run-rate = $18,900 because of lower dashboard usage assumed.

On changing slab size: we allow one slab resize per billing quarter without penalty; prorates are applied pro-rata for the month of change. For reductions mid-term we apply temporary credits for unused capacity in the month of change but not retroactively for prior months. If they want elastic behavior, recommend tracing slab + metered dashboards as hybrid.

Emily — thanks, we can do that. Attached is a concise term-sheet snippet and a worked example for a 12-month slab with a Q2 scaleback to 60% utilization:

- Credit mechanics: if utilization drops below committed capacity for a quarter, we provide a one-time quarterly credit equal to 50% of the unused slab cost for that quarter, capped at 2 months equivalent in the first year. This is additive to any pilot credits we grant.
- Discount ordering: bundle discount (10%) applies to the list slab price first, then term-level adjustment (e.g., 3% for 36-month) applies to the resulting net. We will show both permutations in the term sheet for transparency.

I'll upload the updated term-sheet to the Drive link and notify Procurement. Happy to jump on a call if you want the math walked through line-by-line.
